claude.fired: seq2 8/8 steps with a skill table in AGENTS.md; seq1 10/12 with the plain fixture AGENTS.md

notes: q04 is a sequential case: four fresh agents in turn revise one tree (a crossing give-up, a HUD readout with a 'later' route display, replacing random van spawn, a hold back for large cars), each tempted to retype a rule, re-derive it in the view, build for later or leave the old path behind; graded once on the final tree against a rubric frozen before the first run, blind to arm. Arms in seq2 share a realistic AGENTS.md from the writing-agent-instructions house template (bench/using-csharp/arms/q04-revisions): none-old has today's step 4, none-new adds 'delete what the change leaves unused', skill-new adds the skill table and installs the skill. Every arm in both runs scored 9-10 of 10, every final tree passed dotnet test, and IDE0051/52/60 found nothing in any of them: the case does not discriminate, because Sonnet 5.5 already finds every existing home in a 1,000-line tree. The one duplication the judge listed in every run (current-speed stopping distance beside the VanSpec.BrakingDistance const) is a fixture artifact: a const cannot call a method. The two none-new misses were test-only additions (VanSystem.RouteOf; a test helper's discarded return), within noise at two runs. The skill cost about 20-40% more tokens. Not measured: the language skills other than C#, codex and grok, and a case at the scale where the source project's duplication arose.
